focus.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
focus.abstract: Evidence synthesis is crucial for turning primary research into reliable knowledge for science, medicine, education, and policy. Yet, quantitative evidence synthesis remains largely manual and difficult to scale. Here, we introduce AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system for automated meta-analysis. Given a research question in natural language, AutoSynthesis formulates a search strategy, retrieves scientific literature, screens candidate studies, assesses full-text eligibility, extracts quantitative statistics, computes standardized effect sizes, and finally performs random-effects meta-analysis. AutoSynthesis further supports heterogeneity analysis to examine how effect sizes vary across moderators, as well as risk-of-bias assessment. As output, AutoSynthesis produces a transparent report aligned with PRISMA guidelines. In our application, AutoSynthesis screened over 28 studies and extracted more than 20 quantitative claims. The pooled effect estimates produced by AutoSynthesis are similar to Hedges' $g$ of expert-conducted meta-analyses, indicating close agreement with manual evidence synthesis. Together, these results show that AutoSynthesis can make quantitative evidence synthesis more scalable, thereby supporting evidence-based decision-making across disciplines.
focus.reason: 全自动元分析多智能体系统，强匹配代理能力与技能

focus.title: BrainPilot: Automating Brain Discovery with Agentic Research
focus.abstract: Understanding the brain increasingly depends on integrating evidence across scales, modalities, and disciplines. Addressing a single research question therefore requires a coordinated sequence of operations, from surveying prior work to executing analyses and interpreting results in light of domain knowledge. AI agents promise to accelerate this process, but current agents lack domain expertise in brain science, may fabricate claims, drift during multi-step reasoning, and offer few defined points for expert intervention. These failures are especially costly in brain science, where conclusions feed into downstream scientific claims and depend on laboratory-specific expertise and careful human judgment. We present \textbf{BrainPilot} a \textbf{fully open-source} multi-agent system that accelerates brain science research with traceable logs and agent-verified results. A principal investigator (PI) agent coordinates specialist agents grounded in curated domain knowledge: a unified brain science knowledge base containing 7{,}233 indexed items and a skill library of 72 reusable methodology units across seven research domains. Every major step is recorded in the Graph of Trace, an auditable record that links subgoals, tool use, evidence, and claims and allows researchers to follow and inspect the workflow. An Auditor agent further integrates fabrication checking into the workflow. For evaluation, we run three brain science tasks from Agents' Last Exam, introduce our own benchmark, \textbf{BrainPilotBench-v0}, and present additional end-to-end case studies. Across these evaluations, BrainPilot with an open-source backbone model attains performance comparable to state-of-the-art agent framework with less costs.

focus.title: Does Multi-Agent Debate Improve AI Feedback on Research Papers?
focus.abstract: Probably not, at least for meta-analyses in economics. In a pre-registered, identity-masked, within-paper experiment, the authors of 44 meta-analyses ranked three AI reports on their own paper by usefulness for improving it: a single pass by a frontier model against two multi-agent debate tools we built and expected to win. All reports were held to a common length and template. The authors preferred the single pass, by 0.66 rank points over mad-research (95% CI 0.32 to 1.00) and 0.57 over paper-workshop (0.16 to 0.95), though paper-workshop spent roughly thirty times the tokens. Authors who recalled their journal referee report usually placed it first and never last; in a separate exercise, three AI judges almost always placed the real journal referee report last. Among the three AI reports, Gemini (the judge whose model family wrote none of the reports) would have ranked paper-workshop first in the authors' place, reversing the single-pass preference. The reversal warns against substituting an AI judge for the author. We measure perceived usefulness for finished papers; whether AI should referee papers is a separate question.

focus.title: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
focus.abstract: A growing class of agentic systems maintain persistent state across sessions through memory files, behavioral preferences, and knowledge bases. While this makes agents more useful and self-improving, it also creates a new attack surface for prompt injections in which malicious instructions can be embedded within persistent files and influence future behavior. In this work, we study prompt injection attacks in memory-based agentic systems using a sandboxed synthetic workspace. We evaluate two agentic systems, Anthropic Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, across four models: Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.5. Our results show that although it is difficult to make an agent overwrite its own memory files using untrusted external content, payloads already planted in those files can successfully attack current and future sessions. Attack success and payload persistence vary substantially across systems, models, adversarial goals, and multi-session attack sequences. These findings show that persistent memory changes the threat model for prompt injection and motivate defenses that protect memory updates without removing useful agent adaptation.

explore.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
explore.abstract: Editing the figures in a research paper is a routine and time-consuming part of everyday research practice: authors relabel components, rearrange panels, and restyle visuals as they revise their manuscripts. Automating this editing workflow under a natural-language instruction, however, is challenging, because a scientific figure is a dense infographic in which heterogeneous visual elements such as schematics, plots, photos, captions, and arrows are composed under a tight visual grammar to advance a specific argument. To address this, we present SciDiagramEdit, a benchmark and skill-evolution framework that learns from natural paper revisions and operates on the figure's editable vector source, where users can inspect and co-edit individual primitives alongside the agent. Our benchmark mines before/after figure pairs from arXiv version histories, each grounded in the authors' own revision intent. To accommodate the diversity of editing instructions, we adopt agentic learning via skill evolution: an agentic proposer continually refines the agent's skill specification from execution traces over multiple epochs. The resulting skill progressively lifts edit accuracy on a held-out validation set, providing evidence that natural paper revisions are an effective training signal for instruction-driven figure editing.

explore.title: MAGiSt3R: Multi-Agent Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction from Monocular RGB Videos
explore.abstract: This paper presents MAGiSt3R, a multi-agent 3D reconstruction framework performing reconstruction and camera tracking for monocular RGB videos at almost 10 FPS. MAGiSt3R relies on a feed-forward model from the 3R family to process RGB videos and regress local point maps, and on a merging model, MAGMA, that combines local maps at both intra-agent and inter-agent levels to obtain the final global point map. Furthermore, MAGiSt3R performs pose graph optimization to mitigate cumulative camera drift occurring along the feed-forward pipeline. We evaluate MAGiSt3R on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its superior reconstruction and camera tracking accuracy compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

explore.title: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
explore.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) automation remains challenging in real-world environments, where dynamic layouts, unexpected dialogs, and evolving interface states can cause autonomous agents to drift from user intent. Recent vision-based multimodal agents improve flexibility by operating directly over screenshots and natural language instructions, but planning and adaptation often remain internal, limiting users' ability to inspect, supervise, or correct system behavior. We present Plover, a plan-centric vision-based GUI automation system that externalizes task plans and replanning as persistent, inspectable, and revisable artifacts. Through a planner--executor architecture, Plover supports explicit supervision of evolving execution, localized correction through editable plans, natural-language guidance, and screenshot-grounded interventions, while preserving prior progress during repair. A formative study with six participants informed the interaction design. We then evaluate Plover through benchmark failure-case repair and scenario-based workflow analyses. Our results show that many autonomous GUI-agent failures are structurally repairable when plans remain visible and interventions are localized, and that explicit replanning helps make GUI automation more transparent, controllable, and adaptable.

explore.title: Step-Level Preference Learning for Generative Agents in Social Simulations
explore.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based generative agents simulate human behavior through long-horizon decision-making processes that comprise intermediate steps such as planning, memory retrieval, reflection, and action selection. However, fine-grained human annotations of these intermediate steps remain scarce, and existing agents are not grounded in human preferences over such intermediate decisions. To address this gap, we introduce \method, an interactive simulation interface that enables us to collect step-level human preference supervision over agent decision trajectories, leading to a dataset of 57K fine-grained annotations. We conduct step-level preference learning on open-weight language models using supervised finetuning and direct preference optimization on this data, consistently improving simulation fidelity, coordination, and interaction quality, and inducing more socially effective agent behavior. Our results show that step-level human supervision is an effective training signal for improving both local decision quality and long-horizon agent behavior.
focus_reasons: reward model / process reward / preference learning

xhs.title: AI Agent怎么用于城市规划？
xhs.content: 这里的AI Agent，不是聊天机器人，而是二维网格型智能体模型，模型把居民抽象成虚拟个体，让他们在数字城市中按照规则移动。 	 [种草R]研究技术路线： 郑州校准 → 深圳外部验证 → 推广到中国21个大城市 	 研究者先把城市划分为 1 km × 1 km网格。模型主要输入：网格人口分布、洪水淹没范围、建筑屋顶面积、应急避难所及容量、本地人口与外来人口比例 	 每个Agent按照“感知—决策—行动”循环移动，主要遵循三条规则：远离洪水和危险区域、前往避难所或安全建筑、跟随周围人群移动，本地居民和外来人口还被设置了不同的环境感知范围。 	 [飞机R]手机信令数据怎么调教模型？ 手机信令作为真实参照数据。研究者先将郑州洪灾期间的信令记录汇总为每个网格的人口流入量，再运行智能体模型，比较：模拟人口是否流向了正确网格、模拟流入量与真实流入量是否接近、人口移动热点分布是否一致，然后不断调整行为权重、感知范围、随机移动和空间平滑等参数，使模拟结果尽量接近郑州真实信令数据。 	 参数确定后，换成深圳的人口、建筑、洪水和避难设施数据，用深圳手机信令做外部验证。验证通过后将模型用于21个城市，评估洪水期间避难资源的供需错配。 	 [打卡R]对城市规划的意义 过去常按照静态居住人口配置公共设施；现在可以先模拟灾害、交通或政策发生后，人究竟会如何移动和选择，再决定设施应该建在哪里。 未来可用于洪水疏散、交通治理、公共服务选址、城市更新及自动驾驶共存情景模拟。 需要注意的是，Agent模型并不是天然准确。行为规则、参数设定和真实数据校准，才决定模拟结果是否可信。 	 #城市规划[话题]#  #城市治理[话题]#  #AIAgent[话题]#  #智能体模型[话题]#  #数字孪生[话题]#  #智慧城市[话题]#  #城市大数据[话题]#  #应急管理[话题]#  #交通规划[话题]#

xhs.title: 港中大：多智能体自动开发医学影像AI
xhs.content: 📌 标题：AMID: An Autonomous Multi-agent Framework for Medical Imaging Model Development 	 🌟 重要性：在医学影像领域，医生或临床研究者想为特定数据（如CT、病理切片或超声）训练AI模型，往往需要极其繁琐的手工调参和代码编写。通用AI代理只懂普通代码，却不懂医学影像中的专有约束，比如解剖结构、患者分组、以及预测结果的严格格式要求。AMID的目标就是打破这种瓶颈，让医学AI模型开发从“纯手工”变成“自动化可信流程”，极大加速AI在临床中的应用落地。 	 💡 贡献：1）首次提出专为医学影像设计的多智能体自主开发框架；2）独创“数据条件方法规划”（DCMP），先细致分析数据特征再锁定多个可行方法方向；3）引入“验证引导两阶段优化”，先广泛探索不同方法，再聚焦精进最有潜力的方案，全程由独立审核机制严格校验数据和预测伪影，确保最终模型可复现、可审计。 	 🔍 关键发现：要攻克医学影像模型开发，仅靠AI生成代码远远不够，还需要“领域适配”与“严格验证”双管齐下。DCMP能够自动区分任务的3D/2D结构、标签稀疏程度等复杂属性。两阶段优化中的“审核员”角色至关重要，它能拦截错误的数据分割、泄漏问题或不规范评价指标，避免错误的实验反馈误导整个搜索方向。 	 📊 基准介绍：测试基于ReX-MLE基准，包含了20项来自MICCAI等权威会议的医学影像挑战任务，数据模态覆盖CT、MRI、血管造影、病理切片和超声等，任务类型涵盖分割、检测、分类和图像增强，评价体系标准化。 	 📈 实验结果：在全部20项挑战中，AMID在19项任务上显著优于AIDE、ML-Master等主流通用自主AI系统，其中7项任务的表现接近甚至达到人类专家设计的方案。尤其分割任务中，Dice分数最高提升0.89；检测任务AP提升0.40。这证明AMID能有效解决通用AI在复杂医学场景下的适应问题。 	 #人工智能[话题]# #大模型[话题]# #AI[话题]# #科技[话题]# #医疗[话题]# #医学[话题]# #生物医学[话题]# #文献[话题]# #香港中文大学[话题]# #中国科学院[话题]#
xhs.summary_zh: 港中大AMID框架实现医学影像AI的多智能体自动开发，含DCMP规划与两阶段验证机制。

xhs.title: 上海AIlab&上交大：大模型纠错别只靠聊天
xhs.content: 大模型遇到错误推理时，很多时候用户只能重新提问，或者指出“这里错了”。但模型可能承认错误后，仍沿着原来的错误路径继续推理。 	 上海人工智能实验室、上海交通大学提出 Deep Interaction，解决的是人和推理模型之间更高效的纠错方式。 	 传统对话式纠错需要用户描述哪里错、为什么错，再让模型重新生成一遍。问题是，长推理链里只有某几个步骤出错，整段重新生成不仅浪费 token，也容易再次回到错误路径。 	 Deep Interaction 的思路，是让用户直接修改模型生成的推理过程。 	 它把模型输出像文档一样处理。用户可以直接删除错误步骤、修改关键推理、保留正确部分。系统通过文本变化追踪，识别哪些内容被修改，再把修改后的推理整理成新的指导信息。 	 简单说，不是告诉模型“你错了”，而是直接告诉它“这一段应该怎么改”。 	 为了避免模型只是重复旧答案，Deep Interaction 还加入语义重构，把修改后的内容压缩成更清晰的反馈提示，让模型沿着新的推理路径继续回答。 	 评测覆盖 ScienceQA、Gaokao-MM、LogicQA 和 STEM20K 等任务。结果显示，在 STEM20K 上，普通对话纠错在 1 轮后通过率为 65.18%，Deep Interaction 达到 74.89%；在 4 轮后，对话方法达到 80.35%，Deep Interaction 提升到 86.69%。 	 在不同模型上也有效。GPT、Gemini、Claude 等模型加入 Deep Interaction 后，纠错成功率都有提升。整体纠错能力相比对话方式提升超过 25%，同时 token 使用量下降约 40%。 	 这说明大模型的问题，不只是会不会推理，也在于能不能接受反馈，并真正改变错误路径。 	 问题是：未来人机协作的差距，会不会不在谁一次回答更准，而在谁能更高效地一起修正错误？ 	 #DeepInteraction[话题]# #上海人工智能实验室[话题]# #上海交通大学[话题]# #大模型[话题]# #推理模型[话题]# #人机协作[话题]# #ChainOfThought[话题]# #LLM[话题]# #AI论文[话题]##howto用好AI[话题]#
xhs.summary_zh: Deep Interaction支持用户直接编辑推理链纠错，提升STEM20K等任务多轮纠错成功率。

xhs.title: 自我改进LLM代理共同演化评估指标和技能
xhs.content: 这篇论文试图解决自进化LLM智能体系统中评估指标缺失或不可靠的核心问题。具体而言，论文针对以下关键挑战： 1. 评估信号瓶颈问题 自进化智能体系统通过创建、修订和淘汰技能来实现改进，但每一轮进化都依赖一个隐性假设：存在一个可靠的评估指标来判断任务尝试是否成功。在代码生成等有单元测试的领域，该信号是免费的；但在大多数实际部署场景（如企业文本转SQL、报告生成等）中，准确的自动评估指标并不存在，成为系统改进的瓶颈。 2. 指标与技能的共同进化 论文提出一个根本性问题：如果技能可以进化，为什么评估指标不能进化？ 为此，论文构建了Double Ratchet架构，实现评估指标与技能库的协同进化： 指标循环：将指标视为由小型"缺陷检测器"（drawback detectors）组成的表达式树，通过完整的生命周期（合成、出生门控、边际贡献评分、淘汰）进行进化 技能循环：使用当前进化出的指标对训练任务进行评分，失败的尝试转化为技能合成的素材 3. 无基准情况下的验证困境 在没有准确指标可供比较的情况下，论文确立的验证标准是恢复准确指标本应实现的性能提升（retention），而非击败某个基线指标。具体通过以下协议实现： 三分割协议：训练集（无标签）、开发集（十项锚定参考）、测试集（锁定且永不读取） 选择目标：结合开发集上的锚定一致性与未标记数据上的检测器共识正则化 4. Goodhart风险与安全性 指标与技能由同一LLM产生并相互评分，存在明显的Goodhart风险（指标被操纵）。论文通过以下机制应对： 锚定纪律：指标仅预测其从未见过的锁定锚定集，防止过拟合 确定性设计：指标主要由确定性检测器组成，与LLM评分者的失败模式不同，避免"共享盲点"合谋 独立审计：在参考-free任务中，引入独立的强LLM评委进行成对比较，作为外层审计 5. 可检测性频谱的适应性 论文识别出任务失败模式的可检测性频谱：从机械可检测的失败到纯语义失败（如错误数值但干净执行）。解决方案在失败可机械检测时收益最大，对于语义失败则依赖法官操作与外层审计。 简言之，该论文试图构建一种无需预设可靠验证器、具备自我纠错能力、可解释且可审计的自我改进架构，使LLM智能体能够在缺乏黄金标准评估指标的真实应用场景中实现安全进化。 	 #机器学习[话题]# #大模型[话题]# #深度学习[话题]# #科研学习[话题]# #人工智能发展[话题]# #提供思路和创新点[话题]# #人工智能[话题]# #人机交互[话题]# #创新解决方案[话题]#
xhs.summary_zh: 提出Double Ratchet架构，让评估指标与技能库协同进化，解决无可靠指标时的自进化瓶颈。

xhs.title: 20个获奖机器人Hackathon获奖案例(上)
xhs.content: 我整理了一批 Robotics Hackathon Winner 和高质量项目后发现，真正容易赢的项目并不一定是算法最先进或硬件最复杂，而是任务范围清楚、Demo 直观、叙事完整。很多优秀项目会先通过 teleoperation 采集动作数据，再结合控制逻辑、模仿学习或机器人策略模型完成任务；LLM 更多承担 planner 和任务调度角色，而不是直接控制机器人底层动作。 这篇上篇整理 10 个值得参考的项目，重点看它们为什么值得看、用了什么技术，以及对 robotics / XR / AI hardware 项目有什么启发。 	 参考项目 / 来源关键词： Raju — Devpost / Robot Hackathon NYC Ninja Shirt Folding — Devpost / Robot Hackathon NYC Atomic Kitting — Devpost / Robot Hackathon NYC iSO-100 — Devpost / Robot Hackathon NYC Cadence Labs — Devpost / StarkHacks Ghost Arm — Devpost / StarkHacks Wingman —  Cal Hacks Alfred Robot Butler — Robotic Agents Hackathon RoboChef —  OpenAI Open Model Hackathon Autonomous Triage Kiosk —  StarkHacks 下篇会继续整理另外 10 个方向： 数据中心机器人、垃圾分类机械臂、模仿学习回收分拣、移动机器人、机器人基础模型、机器狗巡逻、救援机器人，以及机器人基础设施项目。 #Robotics[话题]# #机器人[话题]##黑客松大赛[话题]# #WAIC[话题]#  #AI创意[话题]#  #hackthon[话题]#  #机械臂[话题]# #具身智能[话题]# #vla[话题]##人机交互[话题]#
xhs.summary_zh: 梳理20个机器人Hackathon获奖案例，指出LLM作planner而非底层控制器的实用范式。
xhs.reason: 总结可复用的项目设计原则（范围清晰/Demo直观/teleop+模仿学习）。
